issues.description: The sphere-intersection function is declared with a different identifier in the header than is defined and called. In example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h the prototype is declared as "bool check_sphere_hit(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius);" (lines 5-10), but the implementation in example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.cpp defines "bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius)" (lines 10-15), and main.cpp calls ray_sphere_intersect(...) (lines 195-196). This mismatch (header name vs implementation and call site) appears in both the template and the solution repositories and will confuse students and cause compilation or linkage errors if not resolved.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across header, implementation, and call sites. Either (A) change the prototype in example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h to: "bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius);" so it matches the implementation and existing calls in main.cpp, or (B) rename the function definition and all callers to match the header's "check_sphere_hit". Prefer option A to minimize required edits to callers.
